questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Power of a Nilpotent Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
Computing ${B}^{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -9 \\ 4 & -6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 & -9 \\ 4 & -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =O.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, since ${B}^{2}=O,$ the matrix $B$ is a nilpotent matrix of index $2.$ 

We can use this fact to compute ${B}^{5}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{5} & ={B}^{2}\cdot {B}^{3} \\  & =O\cdot {B}^{3} \\  & =O\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{5}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Power of an Idempotent Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
First, we compute ${U}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{U}^{2} & =U\cdot U \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${U}^{2}=U,$ so $U$ is an idempotent matrix.

We can use this fact to compute ${U}^{3}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{U}^{3} & ={U}^{2}\cdot U \\  & =U\cdot U \\  & ={U}^{2} \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{U}^{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{4} & ={C}^{2}\cdot {C}^{2} \\  & =C\cdot C \\  & ={C}^{2} \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{C}^{4}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
